justification: Step 1(1a) claims p13|_{X x {p} x {q}} is an isomorphism onto H_q. This is false when p is not k-rational: X x {p} x {q} = X x Spec(k(p) tensor_k k(q)), and its pushforward to X x {q} under p13 has coefficient deg(p) = [k(p):k], not 1. Hence the correct law is H_p o H_q = deg(p) H_q, not H_q. Step 1(1b) has the analogous error: {p} x {q} x X -> {p} x X is finite of degree deg(q), not an isomorphism, so V_p o V_q = deg(q) V_p, not V_p. Step 2 then uses the false laws: with the correct laws, A o A = sum_{p'} a_{p'} (sum_p a_p deg(p)) H_{p'} and B o B = sum_q b_q (sum_{q'} b_{q'} deg(q')) V_q, but the hypotheses only give sum_p a_p = 0 and sum_q b_q = 0, so the cancellation is unjustified. The cross terms (1c) and (1d) are essentially valid (although the description of {p} x X x {q} as isomorphic to X is also imprecise for non-rational points; the vanishing still follows from dimension drop). The lemma is in fact false: take X = P^1_QQ, p = 0 (degree 1), q a degree-2 closed point, and alpha = H_p - H_q. Then sum a_p = 1 - 1 = 0 and sum b_q = 0. In CH^1(X x X) with basis h = [X x {0}] and v = [{0} x X], H_p = h and H_q = 2h, so alpha = -h is nonzero. Using the correct composition laws, alpha^2 = h - 2h - 2h + 4h = h, which is nonzero. A correct proof would need either to assume all p and q are k-rational, or to replace the hypotheses by degree-weighted conditions sum_p a_p deg(p) = 0 and sum_q b_q deg(q) = 0 and use the degree-corrected composition laws. The opening description of CH_1 as the free abelian group on effective divisors modulo rational equivalence is also imprecise, but not the decisive flaw.
